prompt: Turn three command-line arguments -- number, operator, number -- into a calculation and print the whole sum. Handle a bad argument count, an unknown operator, and division by zero.

explanation: The shell hands each token over as its own element of args, so args[1] is the operator as a String -- which is why the switch compares Strings rather than chars. Checking args.length before touching args[0] prevents an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and each error path prints its line and returns so no result line follows it. Division is the only case that needs an extra guard, because dividing an int by 0 throws ArithmeticException rather than producing a value.
hints: Guard first: if (args.length != 3) print the usage line and return.
Integer.parseInt(args[0]) and Integer.parseInt(args[2]) give the two numbers; args[1] stays a String for the switch.
switch on the operator with cases "+", "-", "*", "/" and a default that prints the unknown-operator line and returns. Check right == 0 inside the "/" case before dividing.
